utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, everybody. Welcome back to this case. Before we have the next witness, there's some procedural matters I would like to discuss with the parties. On the 16th October 2003, the Prosecution filed a motion for leave to ask leading questions of adverse witnesses if necessary. We haven't received any response from the Defence team. Because the time is too short, and we have to move on, I guess that all the parties has already received that motion already. So I would like to spend some time to discuss it before we hear the next witness. Mr. Waespi, would you please brief us about the contents of that motion, please, in a very concise way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. The senior trial attorney will deal with this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Mr. President. This motion was really meant just to be a guideline of what is typically common-law adversarial process. In the event that the witnesses appear to be going in an adverse direction or appear to be arguing with the Prosecution or, as we've described, get sort of legally hostile to the Prosecution, it is our intention to not ask leading questions in the beginning and go through the witness as we would normally. And if it becomes apparent that the witness is not cooperative or appears to be adverse to what they have said before or adverse in some other way, then we were -- would ask leave of Court to ask leading questions if necessary. We want to avoid leading questions if at all possible. But sometimes, with an adverse witness, it's really the only way to get to the point, as the Court is aware of, in cross-examination. It really -- it becomes a situation where the Prosecution ends up cross-examining their own witness. We hope that doesn't happen. But given where these witnesses are coming from and their potential involvement in the case, we just thought it would be realistic that -- to be ready for that possibility. And as such, we wanted to give the Court a little legal background in some national jurisdictions that deal with this. So our -- in the event that there's a problem, our first wish would be to try to refresh the recollection of the witness by letting them read the material to themselves. If that doesn't seem to work, then we would ask the Court if we could go into the more adversarial role of asking leading questions. That's what that's about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any response, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I did receive the motion. I am quite familiar with the concept. It's Anglo-Saxon. In fact all the jurisdictions cited are all former colonies of Great Britain. I don't have any objections to this. There seems to be two distinctions, however, one is refreshing the memory, the other one is asking leading questions of a witness who is called by one party and then is uncooperative, or hostile, as the case may be. Obviously, if a Prosecution's witness, even if not hostile, forgets or misstates something that they have said in their statement, obviously the Prosecution or either party can refresh the memory of the witness by pointing to a particular document. With respect to treating a witness as a hostile witness for the purposes of asking leading questions, usually it's a two-step process. First, there has to be a demonstration that the witness is unwilling to be cooperative. Secondly, they must ask permission from the Trial Chamber to declare the witness hostile. Once that's done, then obviously they can proceed. Had this been brought to my attention without a motion, I would have agreed to it. So I commend the Prosecution for writing this excellent motion on the concept, but I think in the future, we can resolve some of these, and then orally bring them up to the Court's attention. But I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I received this motion from my locker. I took it from my locker yesterday, since I have been away for a few days. And I can just say a few sentences: In the jurisdiction I come from this situation simply is not provided for under the law, because asking leading questions is simply not allowed. But in few of the facts that the Prosecutor has stated and in view of the information we have about which witnesses are coming to us and the significance of their testimony for our defence, the testimony of Lieutenant Colonel Dragan Jokic, we, as his Defence, have no problems with the intention and the wish of the Prosecutor with the permission of the Chamber to ask leading questions. I think that perhaps it would be good, since the Chamber will be making a decision on this, to also, according to the principle of reciprocity, to allow us also if we should find ourself in the same situation, if this happens during our presentation of the case, if you would also allow us to ask leading questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Of course, any decisions on the procedural matters will apply equally to the both parties if in the future the same situation arises. And there's one matter in this situation I would like to draw the attention to the parties. According to the Rule 90(E) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal, a witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. I believe this is the right of the witness. But however, the next sentence says: "The Chamber may compel the witness to answer the question. The testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." So the rule says very clearly that only the Trial Chamber has the power to compel a witness to answer a question which might incriminate that witness. As a practice, all the proceedings should be conducted in accordance with the normal way; that is, try to avoid the leading questions by the examination-in-chief. But anyway, if the Prosecution finds that there is any inconsistency with the previous statement or the witness tries to avoid to answer the questions, the Prosecution should refer this matter to the Chamber, and the Chamber will decide whether to allow this witness to answer that question. And at some occasions, we might go to the private sessions to hear the answer of that witness. By saying so, the motion of the Prosecution is granted. As for the next witness, are there any protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have the next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you hear me? Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. Well, witness, before you start, there's a few words I would like to tell you; that is, as a witness, you have the right to object making any statements which might tend to incriminate yourself. But however, this Trial Chamber has the right to compel you to answer the question. The testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against you for any offences other than the false testimony. So the proceedings, if you find some questions that might incriminate you, please let us know. Do you understand that? I can't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And Mr. Waespi, are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Milinkovic. I would just like to follow-up with what the President has asked you. Do you remember having met with us on Saturday and on Sunday in my office?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And we told you that you could have the right to a counsel and that you had the right to remain silent if you wanted to do so. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: But you said it's fine, you would waive these rights and will be ready to talk to us. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you also said that also in Court, you're willing to go ahead. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So today, you are ready to proceed without counsel in answering the questions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, I would like just briefly to ask you about personal details. Can you spell your name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Milan Milinkovic. M-I-L-I-N-K-O-V-I-C, M-I-L-A-N.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: L-I-K-E, Like.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thanks. Now, what's the date and place of your birth?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st of July 1973 in Ljubovija.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me take you back to July 1995. Were you a soldier at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And to which unit were you assigned?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion, the 2nd Bratunac Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Of which -- any brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you know whether you were assigned to a specific company?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. The 2nd Battalion, the 2nd Company, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, I would like to start with showing you a brief videoclip, and I believe you have seen that back in my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And Your Honours, that's Prosecution Exhibit P148.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you to look at it and perhaps you recognise some familiar faces. And I will ask you later about that. So let's just see the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Are people able to see it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you see something, witness?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could retry it, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If the video -- I think we just continue with the video until we see it, and then we will rewind to the beginning. Please start again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Are you able to see something?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thanks. Let's continue. Do you remember the time and location this video was shot?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that this is the 12th of July in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. I think that's fine. We can stop it here. Your Honours, if we briefly could go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You mean the private session, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think it should be closed because we may be showing a picture which the public outside can pick up from our screens. It will be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that's the problem. It's very brief, but we have to pull all the blinds down. Well, since you request it, we'll go to the closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If we could go on to the next exhibit, and that would be Prosecution Exhibit P22. Again, previously admitted, chapter 10, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone on this picture? And I think you have said that before.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go on to the next image, this is Exhibit P22, chapter 10, page 3. And again, if you could identify, if you may, anybody you know.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: That's me again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: What kind of weapon are you holding?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: A PM, it's a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Was that an official weapon you were given by your superiors, commanders?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. This is a weapon that was owned by my brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If we could go on to the next exhibit, which is P22, chapter 10, page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And Mr. President, this is a new exhibit which we just added during proofing. But it has been part of the bundle which came in via P22.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: It's only a black-and-white picture, Mr. Milinkovic, but perhaps you can recognise somebody on this picture.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I know some of these people by sight. I know this man here, the first man in the picture, in the foreground of the picture. His name is Brano.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You mean the first one on the left side?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you know which military unit he was from?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you recognise anybody else on this picture?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I know these other people, too, but I don't know their names. I know the one with the moustache.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the one with the moustache would be which one from the left side?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Second to the left, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And did you say you knew his name or you didn't know his name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know from which unit he is?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next exhibit, which is again P22, chapter 10, page 5, do you recognise anybody here?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know his position at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: He was with the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let's turn, if we may, to the next exhibit. And this is again P22, chapter 10, page 10. Do you recognise anybody on this picture?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And if we start from the left side, who do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I know this name. He owns a pharmacy in Bratunac, I think. But I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Then the person in the middle, the person with a cap, sunglasses, and a weapon?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Rade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know his last name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the man just right to Jovanovic, do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I do. They call him the "Montenegrin".

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, do you know from which unit these three persons were?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You couldn't tell whether they were from your unit or from somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's asked and answered. He got answer that he asked for. Now he's trying to lead the witness into guessing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Waespi, this kind of leading question is not allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I'll move on. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If we can move on to the next exhibit, this would be P22, chapter 12, page 5. The picture is not very good, but perhaps you can recognise somebody on this picture if we start from the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe I have a coloured picture, and it may be easier for him to get it from the ELMO if we can switch to the ELMO for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. So long as they are the same picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And if you can have a look at it on the machine itself, Mr. Milinkovic. You don't need to look at the screen, but you can turn to your right and look at it. They are numbered. Number 1, do you recognise this individual?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: These are the military police. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you know from which military police he was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The Bratunac military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And if we could turn on to the next picture, that would be Exhibit P46 -- P146, I'm sorry. Thank you. Again, do you recognise anybody on this picture?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is Zaric again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The same person we saw in the other picture before?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next exhibit, and that's Exhibit P147. Here you have two persons, one above wearing a cap, and one below. Do you recognise the person above with the cap?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: That's -- Goran Zekic. Goran or Dragan. Goran.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know from which military unit he was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you recognise --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps the corps police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you recognise the second person, the one on --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And who would that be?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Giga. Milosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So Giga would be his nickname?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If we could move on to the next exhibit, P144, again, the same question. Do you recognise anybody?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Bibic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You mean Predrag Bibic is that person --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And is he on the right or on the left?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: On the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you know the person on the left side?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this picture was taken from?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The old post office in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And was that the same day we discussed earlier, the 12th July?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe a foundation needs to be laid. I mean, he may be able to identify where the photograph was taken, but now he's being asked when it was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. Milinkovic, can you tell us when this shot was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Same objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yeah. Well, Mr. Waespi, you asked this witness when was this picture taken, but you have to lay a foundation that this witness was present at that time or has some informations about the taking of this picture. You know, some background information so that we could whether his answer is just a guess or what he saw at this time, or something like this. In that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Were you with these people around that time on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you said before this was taken in front of the old post station in Srebrenica. Were you in Srebrenica as well --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: -- around that time? Thank you. And was it the same day this picture was taken when you had entered Potocari, what we saw on the video earlier?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If we could move on to the next exhibit, that's 145. Do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And who is this person?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: That's Prebelez, konobar, he's a waiter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: A waiter from which city, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: From Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now we are done with these exhibits, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a few more questions about that day. Do you recall where you were in the morning on 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: In Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, at one time, were you rounded up by some people?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. Leading. I don't mean to be a stickler for formality, but the question is leading. "At one time, you were rounded up." How does he know this? "Please explain what happened on that particular day, walk us through." And then if the person doesn't recall, he can refresh the memory or confront. But I think this is an important witness for some issues, so I would please ask that the Prosecutor be directed not to lead the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, maybe you could put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: On that morning, you said you were in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, where were you in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: In the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were just walking around.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you meet any people?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Only the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how many members of the military police did you meet?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Five or six.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Why do you know these were military police? Were they wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, what did these members of the military police tell you, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: They were shouting at us, and they were telling us to go back to our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, do that? Did you go back to your position?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And who was with you at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Bibic, Predrag Bibic. Bjelov, Bekac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Anybody else?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, where were your positions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The star, the five-pointed Chetnik star. Above Bratunac, there's a hill, a small hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If we could, Mr. President, show the witness the next exhibit, which is P149.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you see Bratunac on the map?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you point with your -- with a pen to the town of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you tell us where you see the hill that you just mentioned where you were positioned.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It's not on the map. There's this, this is nearby. Gradac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The witness pointed to a location about 2 centimetres southwest of the city centre of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me just briefly go back to what you said about these members from the military police. Did you know any member of these military police whom you met on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't know those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were attached to any specific brigade or not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know under whose command these members of the military police were?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Mainly, they were the Serb military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: By "Serb military police," you mean from Serbia or from Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: From Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let's go back to when you went to the hill. How long did you stay on that hill?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps for about five hours, four.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And did someone order you to do something afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Word got through that Srebrenica had fallen, and then we started down towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, did you do that on your own or did somebody order you to go to Srebrenica or to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The commander told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And who was your commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The company commander, not ours, but rather the commander of all of us. Dule, Dule.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And incidentally, do you know the commander of your battalion, of the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Goran Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you said you were told to go to Potocari. And that's when we saw you on that video today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, it's leading, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, for a couple of reasons: One, we have the gentleman indicating that he was in Bratunac, and at some point he's told by the military police to get to -- to go back to wherever they came from. And it seems now -- I mean, now he seems to be leading the witness as to saying well, you're in Potocari because you were given orders. How did he get there? I mean, I'm not trying to be disruptive, but if we could have the witness describe exactly how the day evolved and how he got there, it would be much easier to have a clean record. I'm not sure whether he went back up to the hills, and then was directed back down, or did he initially get the order and instead of going to Potocari ended up in Bratunac, and then was directed back? It's very difficult to follow, Your Honour. And that's why I believe it's leading in nature. It's very unclear. And the Prosecutor is trying to clear up the record because perhaps he's not asking the right questions and we're not getting a clear story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think it's a leading question, but your intervention is helpful. Maybe that's very important evidence in this case. So Mr. Waespi, can you ask questions step-by-step so we can know how this witness got to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I will do so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, you just told us that you were on that hill within your unit.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, when they drove us out of Bratunac, we went back to our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. And from these positions on the hill, you were told by Dule to go to Potocari. Is that what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: How did you get from the positions on the hill to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It's not that far away. It's not a big hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: How long did it take for you timewise?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what were you doing once you arrived in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in Potocari before you went home?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: About half an hour, an hour perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what were you doing in this half an hour, if anything, in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. I was walking down the street. It was an asphalt street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the picture we have seen today on the video, could those pictures be that half an hour you were in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you said you went home afterwards. Where is home for you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: In Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So how did you get to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Once we reached the old post office, or rather, the new post office in Potocari, there were horses there. We took the horses, and we rode off.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: When you say "we," can you tell us who was with you at the time on horseback?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Bibic and myself, Bjelov, Bekac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You mentioned a person Bjelov. Does he have a full name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Mladen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And his last name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And apart from yourself and Bjelov, who else was there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Predrag Bibic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Anybody else?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Bekac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And anybody else? That's fine if that was it.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, do you know from which unit these people were?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The same battalion you were in?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, for how long did you stay in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Four or five days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And were you alone in Srebrenica with your group, or were there other people?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: There were other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what were these people doing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: They were taking things. They were drinking, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And these people, were these civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And from which unit, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you said you stayed in Srebrenica for about four to five days. What happened afterwards? Did you leave Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I went home to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what happened in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I was at home all day in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And for how many nights, if any, did you stay in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Bratunac until the time I was made to go to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, who told you to go to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The housing commission. We were relocated. They didn't do that right away. They did it several months later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, let me just ask a few last questions. Did you ever go to the front line in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did go up there once, and we lost our way. But I don't remember the exact date that was. It was after the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you recall how many days after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Was it a month or was it less than a month?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps a little bit less than a month, something like that. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And who told you, if anybody, to go to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Momir. Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And he was the commander of what, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: He was in the command, a chief of some kind. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you know what kind of unit, if any, he would be commanding?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: He could command everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And my last question: Do you know Momir Nikolic personally?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we know each other. He's from Bratunac as well, so we do know each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I've no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas, we have 10 minutes to go in this sitting. Do you want to begin your cross-examination now, or we have a break, and after the break you could have your cross-examination intact?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why don't we take a break, Your Honour, if that's okay with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll break now for 30 minutes. We'll resume at 10.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave, and I just had asked Defence counsel whether he objected, I would like to ask one more question, an important point to clarify with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Much obliged to my colleagues. I would like to show the witness one page of the proofing summary which we have drafted yesterday when we met with him, and we have, in fact, disclosed that to the Defence, and I think it's now also ready for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. Milinkovic, do you recall having met with me and my investigators over the weekend in my office?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, I would like to show you the second page of the proofing notes which we had drafted. And on the second page, I have marked - it's the B/C/S version - I have marked a sentence in yellow. And in the English version, it's on the second paragraph starting: "The witness further clarified..."

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I would like the witness to read out -- to read for himself, just the sentence from: "The witness did not know any of these individuals." If you can read it to yourself.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us today of which unit was Momir Nikolic the commander of?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: For a while, he was a commander of the military police. Then he became the chief of the command. He was a chief at the command. And I don't know the exact date when he was commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: In relation to the fall of Srebrenica, was he command of the military police before the fall or after the fall or at the time of the fall? Or you cannot tell?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: He was commander of the military police before the fall. Later, he became the chief of security in the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And in the command of what?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The command of the brigade in Bratunac. That's what it would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Milinkovic. Now, back in January 29, 2003, you met with a representative of the Office of the Prosecution, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And as I understand it, you met with them in Bratunac or in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: In Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, it was the Srebrenica police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at that point, you were asked some questions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you provided them -- you provided the investigator with some answers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether that -- how long did that questioning process take place?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps an hour, an hour and a half. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how was it that you were -- you met with them at the Srebrenica police station?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I was called -- they called me at home, over the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And was that on the day that your -- that the -- that you gave the statement, or did they give you some advance notice so that you would know when the interview would take place?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know about it before. It happened on that same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So they called you up, and you went down to the police station, and that's when you met them for the first time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether that statement was tape recorded or not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you distinctly remember not seeing a tape recorder in front of you when you were having this discussion with, I believe it was the investigator, Bruce Bursik?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I take it that there was a translator there or an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did they -- do you know whether at the conclusion of your statement, whether -- or this questioning process, whether they wrote out a statement for you to look at and review?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it they didn't ask you to write out a statement in your words so that we would have an accurate, at least by your terms, version of the events?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, nobody asked me to write anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it that when you met with the Prosecution yesterday in order for them to prepare you for your testimony today, that was first time that you saw the two-page statement or two-page summary that was generated by the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Yesterday, you met with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They asked you some questions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They showed you some photographs and a video?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And they also showed you a two-page summary that had been prepared by the investigator based on their interview with you back in January?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Of course. Because then they asked you to read it and to see if you had any -- if you wanted to make any corrections.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, you made one correction, at least, which was they had put you down to be with the 3rd Battalion when in fact you corrected them and said no, you were with the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it you had the opportunity yesterday to read that little summary, the two-page summary.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And just for the record, that was the first time that you actually saw that summary?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, with the Court's permission, let's go over that summary if we could. And for the record, it's D54/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe we've provided copies to everyone, and if we can give you a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at that and see if you recognise it. You don't have to read the whole thing; just let me know if you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me ask the question again, and I'll do it in a different fashion. When was the first time that you actually saw this summary of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: They did show it to me there, I think, when we finished our conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So now you believe that they had typed it out and then they showed it to you back in Srebrenica at the police station?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, all right. That's all right. And if you don't remember, you know, don't try to make up something. That's the best answer. Okay. Now if we could go through it --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you do remember being there, being asked questions, and giving answers. That you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it when they began this questioning process, they told you that your status was as a witness at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I'm sure they probably asked you to be as truthful and as honest as you could.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And obviously, they probably told you how important it was for you to be truthful and honest at the time because this was a very serious matter. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you understand all the questions that were being asked of you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it at the time that you were answering those questions, they would give you sufficient time to listen to the question, think, and then answer?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And you didn't feel coerced in any way, that you were being forced to come up with a particular answer?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the whole topic of that conversation more or less was about your involvement in Bratunac and Srebrenica during the fall of Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it, back then when you were being questioned, you indicated that on the day that they show you -- they showed you the photograph of you being in Potocari, that was July 12th, on that particular day, you had put in that you were sick. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, if we were to look at the summary, it states that, that you had booked -- that you had booked off sick from duties in the battalion because you didn't want to be on the confrontation line. If you look at the bottom of the page, of the first page, it says that, doesn't it? Look at the last paragraph, the third sentence in the last paragraph. Do you see it, where it says: "He states that he had booked off from duties in the battalion as he no longer wanted to serve on the confrontation line." And then you state: "He admits that he was not sick at the time and was walking through the town centre of Bratunac that morning." Do you see that in the summary?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I take it the investigator put it there in the summary because that's what, in fact, you had told him at the time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I take it you told him that because you believed, at least at that time, that was that was the truth?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just so I'm clear, all right, are we to understand today, here in this Tribunal, in this hearing, that on the morning of the 12th, you were in Bratunac because you had put in that you were sick?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you put in that you were sick, that was an excuse for you not to be at the line?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that excuse was false?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Sick, it was false. It was not true that I was sick.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. All right. But you needed a legitimate excuse so you could leave the line and be in Bratunac and do whatever it is that you wanted to do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't do whatever I wanted to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, that's why you put in -- you fabricated this illness so that you could leave and you could be in Bratunac and have a legitimate purpose for not being where you were supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't want to be on the line that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And now you state that while you were in Bratunac, that's when you were picked up or noticed by the military police?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, today you indicated that you did not know which unit the military police came from. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, are we to understand that the military police could have been from Bratunac, or could have been from the corps, could have been from some other unit?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So as you sit here today, you do not know which units these military police were from, but you believe that they were, in fact, military police?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is there a particular reason why you decided to comply with their requests or their order?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I had to. I had to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why did you have to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: To the line. Because it happened that they would shoot at the soldiers. A friend of mine was actually shot at and wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why didn't you tell them that you were sick, that you had put in for sick and that you were on sick leave legitimately?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody -- they didn't listen to anything or anybody. When they come, they force the elderly and the younger people to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. To go to the front line or to wherever they're supposed to be?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you were in Bratunac, did you have your weapon with you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you would always carry your weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Just like that, you always carried weapons. What do I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you dressed -- were you dressed in your uniform such as it was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Since you were on sick leave, why didn't you have civilian clothes? Why weren't you dressed in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have civilian clothes, so to speak. You just wore uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I understand it, when the military police picked you up, they directed you to go to Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, to go to our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you kindly look at your statement, the summary, now and if you look at sort of the bottom, the last line -- the last two lines where it says: "The Bratunac Brigade military police instructed them to proceed to Srebrenica to assist in its liberation."

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: To the positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, hold on. Do you see anything in there that says "to your position"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. What does it say?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Should I read it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you can read it to yourself and you can tell me what it says, or you can read it out. However you wish to do it.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I thought it was the Bratunac military police, but it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just -- we're going to do it step by step, korak po korak. All right. So you state here, according to the investigator, "the Bratunac Brigade military police instructed them," meaning you and your friends, to proceed to Srebrenica to "assist in its liberation." Does it not say that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, is your testimony today that at the time that you were speaking to this investigator, you had not identified the military police as being from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So that's something that you didn't say, but obviously the investigator must have assumed that that's what you meant.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And then it says that you told the investigator that you were instructed by the military police to proceed to Srebrenica; not Potocari, not to your positions, but to Srebrenica to "assist in its liberation." Did you say that to the investigator, or is that something else that the investigator might have misunderstood and put that down?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I was surprised when they came, when they came for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. But as you indicated, they weren't trying to force you to say something. They were --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, he was a total gentleman when he was talking to you. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You probably had a coffee, had a smoke, he was just asking you some questions. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Of course. And then you indicate in your statement that you entered Potocari around 11.00. If you turn over to the next page in the statement, and I'm referring to D54/1 for identification. If you look at the first sentence in the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Here I have to remind you that in this information report, there's some points that have been redacted. You have to be very careful about certain names if you are going to use them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I wasn't planning on using the names, Your Honour. But I appreciate the cautionary note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do you see where it says that you were instructed -- that you state that you entered Potocari around 11.00?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, roughly speaking. I didn't exactly...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, that was the same date, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course, if you're going to go to Srebrenica, you have to go through Potocari from Bratunac before you can get to Srebrenica. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then you go on to say that you and others were rounded up by VRS soldiers, walked into Potocari towards the large crowd. Is that correct? Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in your statement here, and I take it you read this statement -- you read this information report, whatever it's called, yeah, information report, such as it is. You read it yesterday. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I thought we already talked about how you read it and you made some corrections. You read it yesterday. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: On Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Saturday. I apologise. All right. So you met with the Prosecutor both on Saturday and Sunday?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So for two days, they were prepping you to come here today?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is there anywhere, anywhere in this statement here, where you talk about going back to your location? Why don't you look at it.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Today, you testified when you were being questioned by the Prosecution that you were directed to go back to your position, and I believe it was in Kokarda. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I'm having problems finding that in the little information report that was prepared by the investigator for the Office of the Prosecution. Do you see it anywhere there? It's not there, isn't it? It wasn't there on Saturday or Sunday, so I doubt if it will be there on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That wasn't the question, though. My question is, is it in the information report? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You can't see that because it's not there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, it's not on the information report. And could it be that it's not in the information report because you never said anything like that to the Office of the Prosecution investigator Bruce Bursik?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we only had a tape recording from the Office of the Prosecution when they took your statement.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I think I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But there's no way of verifying of it at this point. Let me ask you this question: I notice that on the proofing notes -- well, we received some -- during your conversations with the Prosecution over the Saturday and Sunday when they were getting you ready to testify here today, did they share with you some notes that they took down to make sure that they were true, accurate, and complete as far as what you had discussed with them and what they had discussed with you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me show you something that might -- let me show you what has been marked as D55/1 for identification purposes. D55/1. If you can please look at it, look at both sides. You don't have to read it, just look at it.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you ever shown this document before coming here today?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: This?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, D55/1, that document.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, let's go through it anyway, or part of it. I want you to look at the second paragraph. And I want you to see where it talks about -- where you correct them with respect to the 3rd Battalion, that it should read "2nd Battalion, 2nd Company of the Bratunac Brigade." Do you see that? First page, second paragraph, third line, do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think you asked this question and this questioned has been answered already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's a reason; I want to lock him into this, Your Honour, because my next question is going to be with respect to other corrections that he hasn't made, at least that are not known in the proofing notes. I just want to make sure that...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you see that, sir? Mr. Milinkovic. All right, listen to my question. In this document I've shown you, I directed your attention to the second paragraph, paragraph 1, paragraph 2. The third line, does it not, in fact, state in your language, in the language in which you can read and write, that you make a correction that in the information report it states 3rd Battalion is incorrect and it should be 2nd Battalion. Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you. Now, in these proofing notes, there are no corrections of you having told the Prosecutor that you were not directed by the military police to go and assist in the liberation of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: They sent us back to our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Listen to me. Yesterday and the day before, is it not a fact that you never told the Prosecution that the information report was incorrect, that you had not stated that you were told to go to Srebrenica to assist in the liberation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it had been liberated by that time, by the time we left our positions and reached Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Milinkovic, yesterday and the day before, you were asked to read the information report and to make any corrections. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I made a number of corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And perhaps you can show me where on the proofing notes, the document that I gave you, which has been marked as D55/1 for identification, the Prosecution has noted that you, in fact, correct the record of what you had said to Bruce Bursik with respect to the military police instructing you to go to Srebrenica to assist in the liberation. Look at the one-page document I just gave you. Show me where it says that you corrected them. You're looking at the wrong document, sir. The one that states: "Proofing notes in relation to Milan Milinkovic," that one, at the top. Read that and tell me where it is that you have corrected the Prosecution. It's the other document that you should be looking at, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The thing about the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Milinkovic, my point is this: With respect to the 3rd Battalion, you correct them. It's quite obvious from paragraph 2. Right? Do you see anywhere else where it says that you corrected the information report by stating that you had not told Bruce Bursik that you had been instructed by the military police to proceed to Srebrenica to assist in the liberation. Do you see that anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And can we conclude from that that it's not in the proofing notes because you made no corrections or offered no corrections to the Prosecution during that two-day period when they were preparing you to testify here today?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, getting back to your information report, the other document, in that document there's nothing in it that states that you had told the investigator for the Office of the Prosecution that you were instructed by your commander to go to Potocari, is there? If you look at the second page --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's nothing in it.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And there's nothing in it because at the time that you met with the investigator of the Office of the Prosecution back in Srebrenica - for the record I'm referring to D54/1 - you never said anything to that investigator that you were told by your commander to go to Potocari on July 12th, 1995? Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. You never told that to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you never told him even after he had instructed you that you needed to be true and accurate and complete with the information that you were to provide him. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't remember every single thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't ask you that question. If the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, if Mr. McCloskey wishes to object, I have no problem with relaxing the rules. He can object rather than shouting to the other Prosecutor to stand up and object. It's a perfect cross-examination, but I have no problem with Mr. McCloskey assisting his colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think you asked enough questions on this aspect, and we know that point is a very important one. But we wonder where you are going to lead us to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it's a slower process than I had anticipated, Your Honour. But as you can see, we're going to get there -- we'll get there. But I'll move on to the next segment, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, don't get the witness confused, you know. Not everybody is quite as learned as you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. That's why I'm trying to break it down as simple as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in your statement, there's nothing in it that states that you were ordered. Right? Nothing in there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you do state that you did, in fact, go to Srebrenica and stayed there for approximately three days.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was. I thought it was three, but it was probably four, five, or six days, or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And now were you in Srebrenica because you had been asked to liberate it, or were you there because you just didn't want to be where you were supposed to be and you wanted to check on your house as well?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It was mostly for the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And you decided to stay there. I assume you were joined by some friends?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, those people that I've named were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And then you started drinking a little rakija, maybe having a little goat barbecue, maybe doing a little looting?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then after four or five days of having some unsupervised fun, you went back to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe in your statement, you state that that's when Momir Nikolic asked you or requested that you go to Zepa. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how many days later. But he did ask, and we did go to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But it's your vivid recollection that it was Momir Nikolic who was -- who instructed you to go to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and of course, you complied with his order.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't on my own. There were soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I take it when Momir Nikolic came up to you and gave you this order, you complied with this order?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't order me specifically, not me personally. The order, who was I? I was a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, how did the order come down? Because you say in your -- in the information report: "Momir Nikolic directly asked me - you know, asked him, meaning you - and those with him to go to Zepa."

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he collected. He got the soldiers together, and we all got into a truck, and then we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But my question is based on your memory, it was Momir Nikolic that gathered you all, put you on a truck and said: "You're off to Zepa"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And from my understanding today from listening to you, that it was your impression that Momir Nikolic was a commander at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Until that time, he was -- yeah, at that time he was a chief in the command. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. A person of authority that could give orders?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And -- all right. Now, in your proofing -- if we could go to the other document, the proofing note, the notes that were generated from the two days of meeting with the Prosecution to prepare you for your testimony here today, here we have a different version. If we look on the second page, and on the third paragraph you state that you were told to go to the hill just above Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe it's the fifth paragraph on the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi, your mic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, thanks a lot. To clarify, earlier, he talked about the Zepa detail from Mr. Nikolic, and now I guess he's talking about the order to go to the hill. So when you say it's a different version, you know, these are two different events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me clarify to make sure that you're not confused. I want to talk to you about the fifth paragraph that's on the proofing notes, and it relates to back on July 12th, 1995. At least, that's my understanding of it. Here, you state that you were told -- that you and your colleagues were told to go to the hill.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to a rock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were they on sick leave as well with you when you were in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You just met up with them in Bratunac? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
