utterances.text: Did they have, like you, a legitimate excuse not to be where they were stationed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you know how it goes. It was one day on the positions, another day at home, one day at the positions, the next day at home. So there was no need for them to be at the positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So they were just hanging around Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: They were off. They could be at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And you were off because you had an excuse, you know, the sick leave.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't actually have sick leave. I just said I was sick, and I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. You self-managed yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I reported there that I was sick, that I was not able to go there. It was like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in your -- in the proofing notes, you say that later that morning, you were told by the company commander Zoran or by Dule to go to Potocari to secure a rock. It states that right there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you say "a rock," "to secure a rock," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Just to be there at that rock. I mean, how do I know what that meant to them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now you say "Zoran." Which Zoran are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Zoran, the waiter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now is it your understanding that Zoran --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: And Dule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, Zoran the waiter, was he your company commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who was your company commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: This Dule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that Petar Dimitric? Wasn't he your commander? It's not in there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Petar Dimitric? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about Jovanovic [phoen], was he the deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you think that this Zoran or Dule were your company commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now Dule, does he have a name, a regular name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you have Like, right? That's your nickname? You have a regular name, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Milan, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Dule, is that a nickname?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Probably. I don't know. Dule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You served with this man?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't with us. He was in some house, but I was in the army there with him in that brigade, in that company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was he your commander or your deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He was a commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Company commander, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He was the company commander for the 2nd Battalion. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you don't know his name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And he was --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Dule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. How long was he the company commander, just so -- I just want to...?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I wasn't there for a long time myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And all this information with respect to Dule telling you to go secure a rock, all of that is something that you told the Prosecution yesterday or the day before for the first time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And of course, today you told us that you were in Srebrenica looting. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: After that, I didn't want to go to that rock, but I went home. So I wasn't there at that rock. I went to see my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And that's where you were -- you went to Srebrenica to do some looting, in addition to checking your house.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not for looting, but to go to see my house, to go and see my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you were also looting for the four or five days that you were in Srebrenica, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't looting. Why would I be looting? What would I be looting with? I didn't even have a car or anything. I just took the goat, and I found some rakija. Had I been looting, I would have something now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The goat belonged to you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: On the road. I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the horses, did they belong to you, the horses that you were riding?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: They were all released. They were all just let out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you characterise yourself, sir, as a well-disciplined soldier while you were serving with the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, were you ever reprimanded for failure to take orders?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So I take it that there were times when you were asked to perform a particular task, and you, being who you are, would refuse?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I was never told by anybody to do anything. I was just a regular soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you ever recall being asked to perform a certain task and telling your commander or your komandir "no," refusing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't go to that rock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let me show you what has been marked as D56/1 for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the record, I'm going to be referring to an English translation as -- though the pages are not -- they don't have regular pages numbers. It's L0073227.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Mr. Milinkovic, if you could look at the top of the page, we have some numbers. And it's 02158994. If you could turn to that page, the last numbers should be 994. I believe it's the fourth page -- or page 5, I believe. And I believe if you look at the bottom of the page, there's a paragraph number 10. And in the English, it would be at the top of the page, again, number 10. Paragraph number 10, if you could look at that.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And -- okay. Now, do you recognise your name there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it you recognise some other names like Mr. Bibic that you referred to today? He's there with you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could kindly read that paragraph, number 10, to yourself just to refresh your memory, refresh it, give it some help.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Have you read it? And the following paragraph, about the whole incident, it goes on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: You don't see that. You can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You cannot read it. Okay. Well, if you go on to the next page as well, flip it over, page 6, the Prosecution -- by the way, sir, Mr. Milinkovic, did the Prosecution share this with you yesterday and the day before when they were preparing you to testify here today? They didn't show you this? Okay. That's where we got it from.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do you -- having read that, is this paragraph regarding this incident dated, I believe, the 28th of August 1994, is it referring to the same Milan Milinkovic who's here today?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So that would be you. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And it talks about you being charged with a crime of insubordination, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It talks about where you were given a direct order by your commander, your immediate -- your komandir, and you refused that order. Does it not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were supposed to go to some position somewhere. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then the chief of staff, I believe, also gave the order; and again, there was a refusal. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we also quarreled with the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, that's my next question. Then even the commander himself came down to give an order to you, the well-disciplined soldier that you told us you were --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Not to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you not -- did the commander not ask you and the others or order you and the others to comply with the order that had been given earlier?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you were aware that your commander was ordering you. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: To go somewhere, to some positions. I don't know exactly what it was, but we didn't want to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You didn't want to go. So you refused your komandir, your immediate commander; you refused the chief of staff; and then you refused the commander himself. You refused to follow the orders. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember if we went when he ordered us to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Well, it says here that you were charged with the crime of insubordination, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it also says that you refuse the commander himself, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, you refused to carry out that order. And as a consequence, that is why you were charged with the crime of insubordination. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so would it be fair to say, sir, that at least during those days when you were serving at the Bratunac Brigade, there were times that you just followed your own orders and did as you pleased and went where you felt like going?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, what did I want to do? The best thing that I liked to do was to stay at home. I did not want to go to the positions. I didn't like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just want to ask a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Milinkovic, good day. My name is Miodrag Stojanovic, and I am defending Lieutenant Colonel Dragan Jokic. I would like to ask you a few things. Do you personally know Major Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever meet this person that you see here whom I say is Major Dragan Jokic then but is lieutenant colonel now, in those few days, in that period?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see Dragan Jokic in that period of July 1993 doing anything in Srebrenica or Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear, if you did not see, that this man Dragan Jokic did anything in that period in Bratunac or Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, nothing. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And one more question: Did you ever hear that in that period, in July 1995, the engineering company from the Zvornik Brigade did anything in Bratunac or Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not hear anything or see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And to end with just one more question: In the interview you had with the investigators on the 29th of January 2003, you said that at the time in July 1993, you were not in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you remain by that statement, that you were not in Kravica at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by that statement that I was not in Kravica at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you don't know anything about those events in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The correct date was July 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect, Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, at this stage, are there any documents to tender through this witness? Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's P144, that's the video still; P145, another video still; P146, another one; P147, video still; P148, that's the videoclip which has been previously tendered, the whole segment; and P149, that's the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections? Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no objections except with respect to P149. I'm not quite sure how a foundation was laid for the map to come in. Obviously, he indicated that first he couldn't locate the place, and then he named one place. But I'm unclear why the map becomes part of the evidence at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, earlier, you know, we admitted all the maps into the evidence. And we used this map, and the witness also pointed out the position where he was at that time, although not that accurate. But it's a place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think there's any big problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I wasn't stating that there was a problem. I was a little confused. But I think you've clarified my confusion, so I withdraw my objection to that. And I have no objections to P144, 145, 146, 147, 148, and 149 to being admitted on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Stojanovic, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dragan Jokic's Defence has no objections or any problems with any of these documents, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Those documents are admitted into the evidence. Are there any documents on the part of the Defence? Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We would move for the admission of D54/1, D55/1, and D56/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: We don't have an objection in relation to the last document, D56. In relation to the two first ones, I thought these wouldn't be exhibits since the witness is here to testify live.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. So the Document D56/1 is admitted into the evidence. As for the other two documents, D54/1 and D55/1, are not admitted into the evidence because as your practice, we have this witness give the testimony here. And I believe that during the cross-examination, the Defence counsel has already used those two documents extensively. It is so decided. Witness, thank you very much for coming to give your evidence. I believe that we benefit a lot from your testimony. We wish you have a nice trip back home. The usher will show you out of the room. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any protective measures for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I believe there will be. The witness will be led by Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please give us some information about the protective measures, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Your Honour. I believe the witness would like all the protective measures including pseudonym, face distortion, and voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I guess there's no objections from the Defence team, so your request is granted. We will have a break and during the time of the break, I believe the Registrar needs some technical preparations, especially for the voice distortion. So we'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The B/C/S booth has technical problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'll try it again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No Serbian interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'll try it again. Well, Witness, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Very well. Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Before we start, I have to tell you that you have the right to object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate yourself. But however, the Chamber may compel you to answer the question. The testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against you for any offence other than the false testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa, the witness is yours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I should just say at the outset, Your Honour, that I will be asking to go into private session at a couple of times during the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please, just let us know when you need the private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, you and I met on Saturday in my office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And at that time, sir, you were informed that you had a right to remain silent and a right to counsel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You indicated, sir, that you were willing to waive your right to counsel and speak to us. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You also indicated, sir, that you were prepared to testify in Court without counsel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, would you please inform us about this witness's pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I could just have the Court's indulgence, Your Honour. P-188.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm going to be asking that we go into private session for the next few questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you entered Potocari, were you attached to a particular unit on the 12th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Why did you go to Potocari that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I was on my way to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And why were you on your way to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: To lock my flat, to lock my house, to keep my house from being robbed and looted. There were lootings.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You're referring to your house in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is there any other reason, sir, that you went to the area that day aside from being concerned about your house and wanting to lock it up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No. No other reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, if there was anything special about the 12th of July for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Well, there were many people in Potocari who had surrendered there, who had surrendered in Potocari. It was strange to see so many people gathered in one place.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What I'm asking you, sir, is there anything of significance to you about the day of 12 of July. Not necessarily 1995, but 12 of July. Is there anything significant about the 12th of July 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes. That's St. Peter's day. It's a Serb holiday, and my father was killed on that day, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And can you tell us, sir, how he was killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: First they killed him, then they set fire to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who are "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: The Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right, sir. And did your unit, sir, that you told us about earlier take part in the operation on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No, we were in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And getting back to when you entered Potocari on 12th of July 1995, can you describe how you were dressed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: NATO, American uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And why were you wearing a uniform that day, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I was a soldier, wasn't I?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You indicated earlier, sir, when you entered Potocari you were not attached to a unit. Can you tell us why you were wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Well, had I not been wearing a uniform, I would have been captured, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. It also appears, sir, from the photograph we've seen earlier that you were entering Potocari with a group of people. Who is this group of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Special police.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know the people individually, sir? Do you actually know their names or who they are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Potocari when you first entered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: About two hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: They wouldn't allow us into Srebrenica, so I went back to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you returned to Bratunac, did you return on your own or with other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I went back on horseback.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. But did you return by yourself or were there others that returned with you to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Most of the people returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did those people belong to the military or were they attached to any particular units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: They were all soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not they were attached to any particular units at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Well, the military police. Mostly they were just ordinary soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not -- what types of uniforms they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: The police uniform and the Republika Srpska army uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So where did you go next, sir, when you returned to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I was on my way to Ljubovija, but I can't tell you when exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you go anywhere else when you returned to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I was walking around town, going to cafes, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you at any point, sir, celebrate the anniversary of your father's death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No. Well, yes, I did go to the cemetery. About 1.00, half past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where did you go after -- or how long did you stay in Bratunac that day, the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: When I returned from the cemetery, I went straight to Ljubovija.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Well, there were cafes that were staying open late over there, so you used to go out there, whereas in Bratunac there was a curfew. And Ljubovija was the place you went to for going out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Did you at some point go back to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: On that day, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Then turning, then, to the next day, the 13th of July, did you on that day go to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When did you go to Srebrenica on that day, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Before noon, in the early hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what did you do when you arrived at Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: We were looting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Aside from looting, did you -- is there anything else that you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: We were drinking, just walking around Srebrenica really.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say "we," sir, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: The whole town was full of people.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you with anybody specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Well, not specifically, not anyone in particular.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Sir, did you at any point go back to see your house or apartment in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Well, that's where I was the whole time. I'd keep coming back all the time, and I'd leave items or things there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are these the items that you were looting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how long, sir, did you stay in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Until -- until the afternoon or evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: To Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what did you do in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: The same thing as on the previous day, just that on that day, I didn't go to the cemetery. We took some of the things that we had brought over to Ljubovija by boat.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where did you spend the night of the 13th of July, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: My house at Mostanice.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you at any point, sir, spend any time in jail?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes, in Ljubovija, but I can't give you the exact date. It was the 13th, the 14th, or the 15th. However, this can be verified.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Turning then to the 14th of July, sir, where were you on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I left for Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what were you doing there that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I was walking around Srebrenica. The same thing as before. You always did the same thing. Whatever was there to be picked up that was worth your while, you would just take it. There was a car there, a Fico.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Where did you spend the entire day, sir, on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Srebrenica. Most of the day, I spent in Srebrenica. In the evening, I was in Bratunac, and after that, I went to Ljubovija, late.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just very briefly, sir, getting back to when you first went to Potocari on the 12th of July, I'm going to show you another photograph marked P22, chapter 10, p2, can you identify the person in this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Milan Milinkovic, called Like.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was he with you, sir, when you entered Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you with Milinkovic before entering Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No. Where -- if I was where?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In Bratunac or anywhere else for that matter. Before you entered Potocari.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No, no, not in Bratunac. Not in Bratunac. We met just before we entered Potocari. On the road, there's a factory a bit further down the road. That's where we met.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: It's a cement factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Getting then back to the 15th of July, sir, can you tell us where you were on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Well, on that day, too, I was in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what were you doing on that day, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: On that day --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: -- well, we were in town, same as usual. I was walking about. I was having fun. At that point, on the 15th, I think they ordered us out of Srebrenica because they were supposed to throw some -- drop some powder from a plane for bugs. And that's why the police told us to leave town.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who are you referring to when you say "us"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I mean, the people from Srebrenica. Milinkovic was there, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you with anyone else on the 15th of July, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Well, I know those people, but I didn't exactly socialise with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you at some point have anybody visit you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: In Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: On that day, on 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: In Srebrenica, whether somebody visited us?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Not necessarily in Srebrenica, sir, but on that day, 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you go -- on the 15th of July, sir, did you go anywhere else other than Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes, to Ljubovija.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you go to Bratunac on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I had to pass through Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you have any friends come visit you in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can just have the Court's indulgence for a moment. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that you gave the investigators a tape-recorded statement, investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor, a tape-recorded statement on the 18th of January 2003. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And sir, on Saturday when you met with me and the investigator, you had a chance to review your statement. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a copy of the statement, sir, and ask you if that refreshes your memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I'm going to be referring to page 13, lines 5 through 7 in the B/C/S portion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's where you should look, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in the English version, Your Honour, I'm referring to page 13, lines 23 through 25.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm familiar with this statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to be directing you, sir, to a particular portion. And I misspoke. It's actually page 14, line 13 through 16 in the B/C/S statement; and page 14, lines 4 through 8 in the English statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just read it to yourself, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Can I say something.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, normally, sir, I'm supposed to ask you questions and you're supposed to answer them. Does this have anything to do with the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes, I've read everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall meeting some friends in Bratunac on that day, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I mixed up the dates. You asked me -- I can't remember. That day came back from Sarajevo, that day, the Panthers came back from Sarajevo, the whole unit came back from Sarajevo that day. So on that day, I met up with my brother and all of the Panthers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know if any of those Panthers are from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: There were just four or five of us from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Turning then to the 16th of July, sir, where were you on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I was in Srebrenica with my brother on that day. And that day, we went to the field in Brcko. We visited Srebrenica, he went to look at his apartment. And that day, our 110 came, and so together we went out in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you go to Branjevo farm on the 16th of July, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you at Pilica on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I passed through Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you in Zvornik on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I passed through Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you tell investigators, sir, when they first interviewed you that you were never in Pilica and Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes. But I did pass through those places. I passed through them five thousand times. I couldn't reach Bijeljina without going through Zvornik and Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So are you telling us, sir, that you lied to the investigators when they asked you those questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. The question assumes facts not in evidence. He indicated that he passed through, so I believe that the question should be rephrased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't see there's any problems. You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So the question was, sir, that you lied to the investigators when you told them that you weren't in Pilica and Branjevo farm on the 16th of July 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I don't mean to be hypertechnical, but I was forbidden from using the word "lie" when they had their star witness here, Momir Nikolic. And so now the Prosecution is using that word. So for consistency purposes -- I don't object to the word "lie," but if I can't use it, neither should they.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You are right. Ms. Issa, better use "false statement," rather than "lie."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I certainly will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Other language is indiscreet.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I take your point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You gave a false statement, sir, to the investigator. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: When I gave my statements, was I there at all?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm going to read you questions from your statement, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't mean to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But if the Prosecution could at least give the witness an opportunity to look at the particular portion of the statement to see whether he accepts that version of the events that are being described as opposed to impeaching the witness at this point. That's what it would appear, because he hasn't committed one way or the other, and perhaps if he could be shown and directed see whether he recognises being asked a question and then giving the answer, I think that would be more fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, that's a good point. Ms. Issa, just point that particular paragraph and ask the witness to read it first. Then you could ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to refer you to page 23 - this is in the 18 January 2003 statement that you gave - page 23, lines 22 to 24 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in the English version, Your Honour, it's page 22, lines 24 through 26 and following.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm also, sir, going to refer you to -- first of all, tell us if that assists you in refreshing your memory.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Well, they asked me the same question there, whether I was in Pilica, and I said no, I was never there. I was never there. They asked whether I had been in Pilica on the 16th of July. I just passed through, but I never was in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So you're firmly telling us, sir, that you were not in Pilica on the 16th of July other than passing through. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you in Zvornik on that day other than passing through?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right, sir. I'm going to show you a map.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: P154, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I would like you, so we can see the places that we're talking about here, show us where you were on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I arrived at Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We're going to be using a pointer, and I'm going to ask you to point out Brcko. If that can be moved down, please. All right. So for the record, you're pointing out Brcko. Can you now point out Zvornik for us, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So for the record, the witness has pointed out Zvornik. Can you point out Pilica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, the witness has pointed out Pilica. And I should say that this map is approximately to scale, and Brcko is approximately 140 kilometres away from Zvornik, and Pilica is under 40 kilometres from Zvornik. So you're telling us, sir, that you were that far away from Zvornik on that day. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think for the next few questions, Your Honour, I'd like to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, this witness is a protected witness. And you have to turn off your mic when you finish your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, you did not serve in the Bratunac Brigade back in July 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, you were with the Panthers, and I think it was from 1992 until well past the fall of Srebrenica in 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I changed two to three units, but I was there very briefly. I spent the longest period of time in the Panthers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And back in July 1995, in particular, around -- between the 12th of July 1995 to, say, the 20th of July 1995, you had nothing to do with the Bratunac Brigade. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I had my own pass which I got from Ljubisa Savic. So I just had this pass that was controlled or checked by the military police, and they would let me through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, your father was killed on July 12th, 1992, which is also -- that day is known as St. Peter's Day. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as it's usual, every year on that particular date there would be a memorial service of sorts for you and your family with respect to your father. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes. And this was done each year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you had a brother that was also serving in the Panthers along with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes, I still have a brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But he was in the Panthers at the time along with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And both of you had made a request to go to Bratunac for the memorial service for your father, but only you received a pass.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes, Mauzer said that we should decide amongst ourselves for only one of us to go because the other soldiers might complain because there were others who also wanted to go home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's how you came to Bratunac, I believe, on July 11th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then that's where I believe your mother was staying at the time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: She lived there. She lived in Ljubovija. Actually, she worked in Fontana, and she began to work in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're originally from Srebrenica, are you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Born there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's where you had your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: A flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course that's one of the reasons why you went to Srebrenica, to check your flat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the other reason was for you along with your friends was to do some looting because the opportunity presented itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it while you were in Srebrenica, looting, you must have been there with some of your friends that you had grown up with or knew from Srebrenica, such as Like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You didn't see him at the time while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I did see him, but he spent time with other people. And those were not the same people that I socialised with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you saw yourself on video, on July 12th, 1995. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were there on your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The Panthers weren't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were never given any orders to go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were never given any orders to separate the men from the women and children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't ask you whether you did it. I'm asking you whether you received any orders.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You didn't receive any orders to participate in any of the events that were taking place in Potocari on that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You did not receive any orders to participate in any activity that went on in Potocari on that particular day, July 12th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, if we are to accept your testimony, you did not receive any orders for the 13th or the 14th or the 15th to do anything with respect to anyone who was located in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Personally, I didn't receive any kind of orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it you did not receive any orders with respect to anyone who might have been situated or detained in Bratunac on the 12th or the 13th or the 14th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I believe you had indicated when you had given a statement that you were able to observe, I believe, on the 13th or the 14th of July that there were men in buses being detained in Bratunac. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you were not involved in those activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you did not receive any orders to participate in those activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the Panthers were not involved, at least as far as you know, with respect to those activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: They weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you did indicate, I believe, in one of your statements that you believe from your observations in Potocari, that Mladic was running the show. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes. I did notice him in the video footage. There was a yellow tape where UNPROFOR units were. And about 15 minutes later, Mladic came.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So just for clarification purposes, did you see Mladic in Potocari on the 12th while you were there, or did you see him in the video? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I saw him on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from your observations of seeing him over there, is that how you came to the conclusion which you gave to the Prosecution, that Mladic was running the operation that was taking place in Potocari on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Well, it's a difficult question for me. I'm just an ordinary soldier, whereas Mladic was a general commanding the whole army. So...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I understand that. But it was my impression that you indicated that he took it all in his hands and was commanding all of the units that were there. Do you recall making a statement to that effect to the Prosecution in your statement that you gave back in 15 March, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Well, I did read through those statements yesterday, but I can't remember every single thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall giving the statement back in 2001? It was a tape-recorded statement. Do you recall giving that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, which year did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: In Banja Luka, yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And did you have an opportunity to look at it yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And did you actually look at it and read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall being asked this question and giving the following answers --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could counsel please refer to the page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm about to do so. And I'm referring to page 17, and I was going to start with line 1. For the record, I'm reading what we'll mark for right now as D57/1 for identification purposes. And if we do have a B/C/S version, I can direct the gentleman to it. It would be page 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could look at that -- if you could look at page 16, at the top part, all the way to line 15 or so. You've read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you see now where you've indicated that it was your understanding that General Mladic was making all of the decisions and commanding all of those units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: But that was my understanding of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's all I'm asking for. Based on what you saw --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: That's just an assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Was that assumption made on the basis of what you saw, or were you just saying anything that came to the top of your head when you were giving this interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No. When he came, everyone obeyed him. He was saying something, and everyone just gathered around him instantly, and they were all listening to him, the commanders.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Karnavas, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from your observation, you were under the impression that Mladic was in control and commanding all of these units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you were in Srebrenica off and on -- or I should say Bratunac, Srebrenica off and on during the July 12th, 13th, 14th, and 15th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You would stay at home with your mother. Right? That's where you were living at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: We lived in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then you would go to Srebrenica during the day. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Have some fun with your friends, visit your house, do a little bit of looting, drink some rakija. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then go back to Bratunac, but then go off to Ljubovija because that's where the nightlife was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do a little more partying, a little more drinking, and then go back to mom's for a little more sleep. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I'd go back to my own place, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your own place. Okay. Basically, that was the routine you had for all of those days up until the morning of the 16th. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Then on the morning of the 16th, I believe that is when your unit, the Panthers, came to Bratunac and you saw them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No, not units. Only the lads who were from Bratunac came, and the units had left for Bijeljina first, and then left for Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're right. And one of the lads was your brother? Right? One of the lads from Brcko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so you and the lads at some point got into a truck to take you to Brcko. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, and this was on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I believe that you left Bratunac sometime in the morning of the 16th, or mid-morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in order to go from Bratunac to Brcko, you have to pass -- the road passes by Zvornik. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then if you go past Zvornik, a few kilometres away, there's Pilica. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, right on the road is where there's the dom kultura of Pilica, or are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And before you get to Pilica, there's a turn that you would take that would be on the left side, and you would go up a small hill, and that would take you to Branjevo farm. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then if you continued on the road, you would end up in Bijeljina. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: There's only the main road. You don't turn off anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. You would take -- you would stay on the road, pass Zvornik, you continue, it takes you to Bijeljina. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's where you have to make a turn to go towards Brcko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: We go to our barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But as I understand it, you were heading towards Brcko because that's the orders that you and the lads had gotten. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Wherever you went on a mission, you had to report to the barracks, and the barracks was in Bijeljina. And it was from Bijeljina that I later went to Brcko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: One or two more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, let me get my thought again. Okay. Now when you went -- when you left -- when you left Bratunac on that particular morning, when you say "the lads," we're talking about the lads from Brcko. Right? I mean from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So all of you were dressed in soldiers' uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Carrying your weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were heading from Bratunac through Brcko, passing through Zvornik and passing through Pilica. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: How should I first go through Brcko and then pass through Zvornik? I don't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're going through Brcko and then --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Karnavas, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can explain using a map if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand the geography. You had to go to Brcko, but first you had to pass through Zvornik. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: There's only one road there. There's no other road really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that road takes you by Pilica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the time that it would take you to go from Bratunac to Zvornik, how long would it take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: About 50 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then another 5 minutes or so from Zvornik to get to Pilica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as far as you're concerned, the medical records stating that you were in that vicinity on the 16th of are incorrect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: One last question: When you and the lads from Bratunac of the Panthers were on their way to go to Brcko, were there any members with you from the Bratunac Brigade that were also heading towards Brcko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188
utterances.text: No, we were picked up by our lorry that had arrived from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no more further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I do have one question, Your Honour, if I can just have a moment's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Issa, I think you finished your direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I couldn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I just want to ask, your question is addressed to me or to the witness? If to the witness, I think you are finished your question, your direct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I thought Your Honour was asking me whether or not I had any re-examination questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, not yet. It's time for the break. Maybe tomorrow you still have the chance.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Witness, I'm afraid you have to be here in The Hague for another day. And during your stay here, you're under the oath. So do not talk to anybody about your testimony, and do not let anybody talk to you about it. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And please remain seated. And later on, the usher will show you out of the room. We'll resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
